# Marky v1.8.8

Two Git sync fixes, both in paths that had never been exercised by automated tests.

### Git sync

- Fixed the Windows askpass helper mangling SSH key passphrases containing `%`, `&`, `|`, `<`, `>`, `(`, `)`, `"` or `^`. Those characters are syntax to the Windows command interpreter, so a passphrase using any of them was truncated or rejected, and `&` caused the rest of the passphrase to be run as a command. Passphrases are now escaped before the helper echoes them. A passphrase of exactly `off`, or one with a leading space, is also passed through intact now. macOS and Linux were unaffected.
- Fixed merge commits ignoring the author configured in Marky's sync settings. Merges were left to git's own identity lookup, so the merge commit was attributed to whatever the machine's global git config happened to say — and on a machine that has never had `git config --global user.name` set, syncing an edit made on a second device failed outright with `empty ident name`. Merge commits now use the same identity, and the same neutral fallback, as every other commit Marky writes.

### Release reliability

- Rust compilation is now checked on Windows in pull-request CI. Checking only on Linux never compiles `#[cfg(windows)]` code at all, which is how the v1.8.6 desktop builds broke.
- The Rust test suite now runs in CI. It previously ran nowhere, which is why the merge-identity bug above went unnoticed.
